title: Donor Retention
disclaimer: Synthetic training document for an educational project. Not an official policy, report or donor record of any real organization.
content:
Donor retention focuses on maintaining long-term relationships with existing donors. Keeping an existing donor is usually far less expensive than acquiring a new one, so retention is one of the most important health indicators for a humanitarian fundraising programme.

The retention rate is the share of last year's donors who give again this year. Teams should track retention separately for first-time donors, repeat donors and monthly donors, because first-time donors are the most likely to lapse.

To improve donor retention, thank every donor quickly and personally, ideally within 48 hours of the gift. Send regular impact updates that show what the donation achieved, for example how many families received clean water or how many children were vaccinated. Be transparent about how funds are spent, including administrative costs.

Personalized communication improves retention. Use the donor's name, reference their previous gifts and respect their preferred channel and frequency. Avoid sending too many appeals; donor fatigue is a common reason for lapsing.

A structured stewardship journey helps new donors. A welcome series after the first gift, a mid-year impact report and an annual appreciation message build trust. Inviting donors to feedback surveys shows that their opinion matters.

When donors stop giving, run a reactivation campaign for lapsed donors with a clear, emotional story and an easy way to give again. Converting one-time donors into monthly donors is one of the strongest ways to improve long-term retention.
